newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.

text.p: Early calls on both CME live and feeder cattle futures ranged from 0.100 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower ahead of the USDA Cattle-on-Feed Report, analysts said.
Mixed trade is expected to prevail in both pits as traders take to the sidelines awaiting the monthly report, they said.

On-feed estimates averaged 115.6 percent and ranged between 114 percent and 117.8 percent for the major seven states in the report. Placement estimates averaged 100.8 percent and ranged from 96 percent to 106.5 percent and marketings averaged 105.5 percents and ranged from 103 percent to 107 percent of a year ago.

Recent firmness in fed cattle markets and the upturn in boxed beef values were considered supporting factors in live cattle. Feedlots were seen asking $66 to $67 per cwt for fed cattle next week and beef demand for Labor Day was expected to rise. But the report will take precedence, they said.
USDA reported boxed beef values up $1.33 to $0.40 per cwt Thursday afternoon.

A lower CME feeder cattle index may put some pressure on feeder cattle but action in corn futures will again be the driving force. However, trade is light as the market awaits the cattle report, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.29 at $80.90 per cwt.
